blocks.body:
# EDG Organic Search CTR & Position Audit — July 13, 2026

**Decision:** fix measurement distortion first, then run one contained restaurant-patio page pilot while protecting the already-successful MagnaTrack cost queries.

Read-only audit of `sc-domain:edgpatioshade.com`, Web, April 12–July 11, 2026, with the latest 28 days compared with the previous 28 days. Signed-in data was read in the existing Comet profile; production pages were checked in the Codex in-app Browser.

## Executive diagnosis

EDG's three-month headline is better than the previous three months: 1,042 clicks versus 370, about 95.8k impressions versus 47.0k, CTR 1.1% versus 0.8%, and average position 17.3 versus 24.7. That improvement is real, but the current trajectory is weaker. In the latest 28 days clicks fell to 357 from 437 while impressions rose to 35.7k from 30.2k; CTR fell to 1.00% from 1.45% and position worsened to 20.9 from 16.0.

Two effects are mixed together. First, at least 16,829 three-month impressions came from 262 visible, templated zero-click query rows that look like automated rank tracking or measurement activity. One exact phrase generated 3,696 impressions, almost entirely on desktop, during a short April 28–May 15 burst. Those rows make the property-wide CTR and position less useful as a pure customer-demand KPI. Excluding only the flagged rows produces an indicative 1.32% CTR, but that is a diagnostic—not a replacement for Google's official metric.

Second, genuine pages lost rank or expanded into weaker query mixes after mid-June. The MagnaTrack cost guide, the www homepage, and `/systems/shades` account for most of the recent click loss. At the same time, relevant category and local routes often do not own the queries they should: broad pergola and near-me queries map to the homepage, while cost/screen queries split between the shades service page and the cost guide.

The visible query export is directionally non-brand: EDG-branded rows contributed 52 clicks from 516 impressions, while non-EDG-branded rows contributed 293 clicks from 48,011 impressions. Because Search Console omits anonymized queries and limits rows, these are not property-wide shares. The United States is the clear market focus at 90,104 of 95,765 impressions and 994 of 1,042 clicks.

## What changed recently

- `/guides/magnatrack-screens-cost`: 187 clicks versus 223, despite 8,410 impressions versus 7,284; CTR fell 0.84 percentage points and position worsened from 5.94 to 8.14. The exact query `magnatrack screens cost` actually improved to position 2.85 and 7.33% CTR, so the page-level decline comes from a broader, lower-ranking query mix—not failure of the head term.
- `https://www.edgpatioshade.com/`: 35 clicks versus 51, with impressions up by 1,131 and position worsening 6.08 places to 34.79.
- `/systems/shades`: 32 clicks versus 51; position worsened from 17.80 to 26.27.
- `/guides/pergola-cost`: impressions increased by 2,237 and clicks rose by eight, but position worsened from 6.88 to 18.46. This is growth into a much broader, weaker ranking mix.
- Both major devices weakened. Desktop CTR was 0.69% versus 1.00%, and mobile CTR was 1.35% versus 2.14%. Desktop is more distorted by suspected automated activity, but mobile deterioration proves the recent decline is not only a bot artifact.

## CTR opportunities

1. **Separate price intent from system intent.** For `motorized retractable screens price`, `/systems/shades` received 260 impressions and two clicks, while the MagnaTrack cost guide received only 93 impressions but the same two clicks. For `magnatrack screens`, the guide earned nine clicks from 529 page impressions while the service page earned three from 657. Make the guide the explicit cost/price owner and the service page the installed-system/fit owner through titles, H1s, copy, and internal-link anchor text.
2. **Do not rewrite the winning MagnaTrack head-term snippet.** `magnatrack screens cost` improved to position 2.85 and 7.33% CTR in the latest 28 days. Preserve that title/description promise; improve the broader supporting query coverage around it.
3. **Use the restaurant cluster as the first clean snippet/content pilot.** The singular/plural enclosure and patio-cover cluster produced at least 706 visible three-month impressions at roughly positions 17–19 with zero clicks, and the correct route already owns nearly all of the impressions.
4. **Treat desktop CTR after removing suspect query families.** Baseline desktop CTR was 0.75% versus mobile at 1.60%, but automated impressions were overwhelmingly desktop. Compare clean query cohorts before making device-specific design conclusions.
5. **Protect structured-data truth.** Historical Product snippets were weak at 0.53% CTR and position 24.2; Merchant listings were strong at 4.39% CTR and position 1.35. All came from `/systems/shades`. The live page now correctly uses Service/HowTo/FAQ markup after unsupported Product/AggregateOffer/AggregateRating markup was removed July 7. Do not restore invented offers or reviews to chase merchant visibility.

## Ranking and average-position opportunities

1. **Restore authority to the pages already closest to page one.** Prioritize the MagnaTrack guide, restaurant patio enclosures, and the pergola cost guide with materially useful updates, proof, and internal links—not mass new pages.
2. **Fix route ownership.** The broad query `pergola` ranked 4.38 with 632 impressions, but nearly all visible impressions mapped to the non-www homepage; `/systems/pergolas` had one. `motorized pergolas near me` mapped primarily to the www homepage and not to `/systems/pergolas`. Strengthen category and local-route signals from the homepage, system hub, service-area hubs, and related guides.
3. **Make geographic pages earn their intent.** For `deerfield il motorized porch screens`, the non-www homepage received 226 page impressions while the exact Deerfield retractable-screens route received seven. Review internal linking, unique local proof, and duplication across local templates before adding more city pages.
4. **Consolidate legacy URL signals.** The live non-www host 301s to www and live canonicals/sitemap use www, but Search Console still reports separate homepage host rows. Old non-www WordPress routes can require multiple redirect hops. Monitor URL Inspection and simplify redirect chains where it can be done without breaking mappings.
5. **Expand cost guides around evidence, not keyword lists.** `/guides/pergola-cost` is earning many new impressions at weaker ranks. Add real installed-project examples, range assumptions, comparison tables, permit/engineering factors, and links from the pergola system and local-market pages.

## Recommended first pilot: one commercial page, one query cluster

Pilot `/commercial/restaurant-patio-enclosures` for the regex cluster `restaurant patio enclosure|restaurant patio enclosures|restaurant patio cover`. The route already owns the impressions, so the test is cleaner than changing the homepage or the two competing screen pages.

After approval, keep the scope to one page: align title and H1 with Chicago restaurant patio enclosure intent; add one source-backed project/proof section; tighten the first-screen copy around seating, weather protection, permits, and operations; and add three to five contextual internal links from the commercial hub, restaurant-solutions page, relevant system pages, and a real project page. Do not add Product/Offer/review schema.

**Success threshold:** wait for at least 500 post-change cluster impressions and at least 28 days after Google recrawls. Call it a win if average position improves by at least two places without losing impressions, or if CTR rises by at least 0.5 percentage points at a comparable position band. Use exact page + regex query filters; do not judge from the property-wide average.

## Quick wins, medium-term changes, and experiments

### Quick wins — first 1–2 weeks after approval

- Build a clean Search Console reporting view that excludes the flagged templated query families and reports branded, non-branded, local, screen, pergola, and commercial cohorts separately.
- Confirm whether any SEO vendor, rank tracker, or internal automation generated the suspicious phrases. Disable or throttle it if possible; do not alter customer-facing pages around those phrases.
- Run the restaurant-page pilot and preserve the current winning MagnaTrack cost-title promise.
- Capture URL Inspection status for www and non-www homepage variants and the top legacy routes; this is separate from deployment proof.

### Medium term — 4–8 weeks

- Establish explicit route ownership for screen cost versus screen service intent, and for pergola category versus local-market intent.
- Strengthen internal links to `/systems/pergolas`, `/systems/shades`, the two cost guides, and the commercial restaurant route from high-authority hubs and relevant project pages.
- Add real project evidence and decision-useful comparisons to pages with growing impressions but positions 8–20.
- Review local templates for unique proof and remove or consolidate thin overlap before creating more location pages.

### Controlled experiments

- Title/description test on the restaurant page only; compare against the fixed query cohort, not sitewide CTR.
- Internal-link anchor test for `/systems/pergolas` from homepage/system/local hubs.
- If EDG later has accurate product pricing, availability, and review data, validate a compliant Product/Merchant implementation in a non-production test before considering eligibility restoration.

## Measurement plan and guardrails

- **Freeze baselines:** retain the attached three-month, recent-28-day, query-page, device, country, and search-appearance exports. Record the approval and deployment dates for any later change.
- **Use fixed cohorts:** report exact page + query regex cohorts weekly. Keep branded and non-branded separate; exclude flagged suspect templates in a second clean view while preserving official unfiltered totals.
- **Compare like with like:** CTR is only interpretable within comparable position bands. Track positions 1–3, 4–10, 11–20, and 21+ separately.
- **Wait for enough data:** use at least 28 days and 500 impressions per pilot cluster when possible. Annotate recrawl/index dates; avoid reacting to the first few days.
- **Primary outcomes:** clicks, CTR, impressions, and average position for the target page/query cohort. **Guardrails:** total page impressions, conversions from organic sessions, branded clicks, rich-result eligibility, canonical host, and unintended cannibalization.
- **Schema guardrail:** review search-appearance rows after the July 7 schema cleanup, but do not use rich-result recovery as a success criterion unless the underlying data is accurate and eligible.
- **Limitations:** Search Console query tables omit anonymized rows and can be row-limited; page rows may be non-additive; average position is not a rank-tracker reading; suspected automation is an inference from pattern, timing, device, and zero-click behavior—not a confirmed identity.

## Source and live-site cross-check

The production pages returned live canonical URLs on the www host and the sitemap contains every route named in this audit. The non-www root returns a 301 to www. The homepage, shades, MagnaTrack cost, pergola cost, pergola system, and restaurant enclosure titles/descriptions match current source. Live JSON-LD types are Service/HowTo/FAQ on shades; Article/FAQ on the MagnaTrack cost guide; Article/FAQ/HowTo on the pergola cost guide; Service/FAQ on the pergola system page; and Service on the restaurant page.

Current source also confirms that the homepage uses a broad pergola/screens title, the category and guide pages cross-link, and legacy WordPress paths have path redirects. The redirect rules do not define the host redirect; Vercel currently supplies it. Supporting CSVs, screenshots, manual query-page observations, and the executed analysis notebook are stored beside this report under `docs/codex/`.

query.engine: DuckDB over Google Search Console CSV
query.sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT CAST(Date AS DATE) AS date, CAST(Clicks AS DOUBLE) AS clicks, CAST(Impressions AS DOUBLE) AS impressions, CAST(Position AS DOUBLE) AS position FROM read_csv_auto('docs/codex/organic-search-ctr-position-audit-2026-07-13-evidence/last-3-months/Chart.csv', header = true)) SELECT CAST(date_trunc('week', date) AS VARCHAR) AS week_start, SUM(clicks) AS clicks, SUM(impressions) AS impressions, SUM(clicks) / NULLIF(SUM(impressions), 0) AS ctr, SUM(position * impressions) / NULLIF(SUM(impressions), 0) AS position FROM daily GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
query.description: Property-level daily Web performance exported from the signed-in Search Console Performance report.
metric_definitions: Average position is Search Console's impression-weighted topmost result position
